title: Samsung Plans to Bring More 2-Nanometer Chipmaking to Central Texas
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Samsung Electronics is moving ahead with a second semiconductor fabrication plant in Taylor, Texas, as part of a planned investment of more than $37 billion across Central Texas. Samsung targeted November 2026 for construction to begin on Taylor Fab 2 and aims to start mass production in 2030. The new facility is planned alongside Samsung’s first Taylor fab, with both plants forming part of a broader expansion that includes a research and development facility in Taylor and upgrades to Samsung’s existing Austin operation.

Samsung officials say Fab 2 will manufacture chips using 2-nanometer technology. The U.S. Department of Commerce awarded Samsung Austin Semiconductor up to $4.745 billion in direct funding under the CHIPS and Science Act to support the wider program. Samsung expects the two Taylor facilities to support roughly 3,500 direct jobs once both are operating.

Why it matters

A second Taylor fab could give chip designers another U.S. option for manufacturing advanced logic used in products such as AI accelerators and data center processors. Bringing another facility online would add geographic diversity to the supply chain and give customers more flexibility when planning where to manufacture future chip generations. Those benefits depend on Samsung reaching volume production and customers qualifying their designs for the process.

For Central Texas, the opportunity extends beyond the cleanroom. Two production fabs and a nearby research facility could sustain demand for equipment servicing, specialty materials, and skilled technicians. Samsung can also draw on decades of operating experience in Austin as Taylor scales. Over time, the concentration of research, manufacturing, and suppliers could help the region develop the technical workforce and industrial capacity needed to support successive generations of advanced chips.
